evidence: The reviewer's own output on this PR still signs "## CoPirate Code Review" with a `<!-- copirate-code-review-agent -->` marker as late as round 1 (2026-09-27), so the deployed action's identity disagrees with the renamed docstring; the packet cannot show whether the upstream repo was renamed, which is why the premise is partly. The thread was resolved with no reply and no commit touches the docstring, so the agent never answered which was true.
guidance_note: When renaming an external dependency in docs, grep the repo for the old name (workflow pins, source citations, test fixtures) and rename all of them or none in the same commit.

evidence: The hunk shows "Two ship today" with only `action` and `local` above "The contract for writing a fourth is in". The thread was resolved without a reply or a fix, and the same line comes back as F13 in round 1.
guidance_note: When deleting an entry from an enumerated list, reread the surrounding prose for counts and ordinals derived from it ("Three ship today", "a fourth") and update every one.

evidence: Both edits are in this PR: step 2 now reads "make it a synchronous no-op if `fetch` blocks" while the wait() error message (F5's hunk) reads "If the local agent runs synchronously inside trigger(), implement wait". That is a real contradiction inside one stub. Resolved silently, with no fix.
guidance_note: When rewording one statement of a contract, grep the touched files for every other statement of the same contract (here fetch vs trigger) and make them name the same function.

evidence: The PR deletes action_provider.test.py outright, and its fake-gh `wait() end to end` cases were the only callers of ap.wait. F12 confirms that after the merge, nothing in the test file calls wait. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: When deleting a test file because the feature it mainly covered is removed, keep or rewrite the cases that drive surviving functions (wait's polling and return shape) without the removed assertions.

evidence: This is the same contradiction as F3, seen from the wait() side. The stub still says "synchronously inside trigger()" after PROVIDER_CONTRACT.md's wait section was narrowed to fetch. No reply and no fix.
guidance_note: When removing the module a doc used as its example (adversarial_provider), sweep every doc that pointed to that example and restate the guidance against the contract that remains.

evidence: This duplicates F4: deleting the whole test file removed the only wait() happy-path test along with the verdict tests, and F12 shows the gap still open after the merge. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: Before deleting a test file, list which of its cases exercise code that survives the change, and keep those.

evidence: github_threads.py shows `def bot_reviews(...): return paginated(...)`, so bot_reviews calls paginated, not the reverse, and the changelog sentence has the direction backwards. The 4917f8f CHANGELOG context still carries the unchanged sentence.
guidance_note: Before writing a changelog claim about which function reads which, open the call site and check the direction of the call.

evidence: After this PR, wait() returns `sha` for any completed run, including one whose round cap was spent, so "the head SHA that was reviewed" claims more than the code guarantees. The replaced wording, "the head SHA the run was for", was accurate. No reply and no fix.
guidance_note: When reverting a guarantee, check each doc line the revert edits against what the code now guarantees, and keep the narrower wording where the older one overclaims.

evidence: head_review_verdict is deleted, but github_threads.py still describes bot_reviews as serving "the dismiss set and the reviewed-verdict alike". The round-1 summary re-raises the identical body finding at github_threads.py:250, so the thread was resolved without the comment ever being changed.
guidance_note: When deleting a named concept, grep the whole repo for its name ("reviewed-verdict"), including files the diff does not touch, and fix every dangling reference in the same commit.

evidence: The capped-run behavior the reviewer calls a silent failure is the PR's stated purpose. The CHANGELOG says "the cap is a cost control the repository sets deliberately, and a loop that treats its own budget being spent as an error stops every PR that reaches the limit", so the S5 needed a recorded pushback; instead the PR merged with it unanswered. The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: 4917f8f is a merge of master that does not touch wait(), and the deletion it flags is in the original PR diff.
guidance_note: When a PR deliberately removes a safety check, state the accepted consequence in the code comment at the removal site (a capped run reads as clean), so a reviewer reading the diff sees a decision rather than a regression.

evidence: After 4917f8f the module docstring names coding-agent-review, while the body-findings code merged in from master cites "copirate-code-review-agent src/transport.js" twice. The test fixture also models the CoPirate heading and marker, so the file contradicts itself. The flag is a false positive for fix-causation: 4917f8f merged master and fixed no finding. It is the unanswered F1 rename question meeting new code from master.
guidance_note: After merging the base branch into a PR that renames something, grep the merged result for the old name again, because the base brings in new references the rename never saw.

evidence: The 4917f8f test file (from master) has fake-gh cases only for parse_body_findings, body_findings and fetch; nothing calls ap.wait. This is the gap F4/F6 raised in round 0, still unaddressed. The flag is a false positive: the merge restored the file from master, and losing the wait cases is the original PR's deletion, not the result of any fix.
guidance_note: Same move as F4: when removing tests for a deleted feature, keep a case that drives each surviving entry point.

evidence: This is F2 verbatim ("a fourth" under a two-provider table), raised again because F2's thread was resolved without any change. The flag is a false positive: no fix was attempted, so this is not an incomplete fix, and the line is unchanged since round 0.
guidance_note: Never resolve a thread without either a pushed fix or a reply stating why no change is needed; a silently resolved finding comes back next round.

narrative: The PR reverts the reviewed-verdict mechanism and removes the adversarial provider. Round 0 raised nine findings: mostly real doc drift (stale counts, a fetch/trigger contradiction, a backwards dependency claim, dangling reviewed-verdict references) plus lost wait() test coverage. Every round-0 thread was resolved by the author with no reply and no fix. The only later commit, 4917f8f, is a merge of master (ceiling grace, body findings, the --reset removal), so round 1 repeated F2 and F9, again raised the missing wait tests, flagged the rename against the copirate citations that came in with the merge, and raised an S5 against the PR's deliberate design. The PR merged with every round-1 thread open and unanswered.
guidance_observations: Round-0 threads were resolved with no plan comment and no fix, against the address-pr-reviews rule to post a plan on every thread; that silence is the whole reason F13, F12 and the github_threads body finding came back.

The PR merged over an open CHANGES_REQUESTED review that included an S5, with no recorded disposition for any round-1 finding, even though the S5 had a clear, defensible pushback in the PR's own CHANGELOG.
Merging master into the branch mid-review triggered a re-review of unrelated code and introduced new inconsistencies with the PR's rename (F11); a rename PR needs a re-sweep after every base merge.

evidence: The PR removes `--reset compact` and the tmux worker now only sends /clear, so "The tmux transport compacts in place" is the wrong verb. The thread is outdated, the author's issue comment lists "stale compact comments" among the fixes, and the next round approved. The thread itself got no reply and was left unresolved; the packet does not include the fixing diff.
guidance_note: When retiring a mode (compact), grep comments and tests for its verb ("compacts", "compact"), not just the flag spelling, before pushing.

narrative: This PR drops the --reset flag so that every finalize-session run resets. CI raised one S1 comment-drift finding, which the author fixed during a local high/medium/low review cycle recorded in issue comments, and the next two CI rounds approved. No finding came from a fix.
guidance_observations: The fix was recorded only in a PR issue comment; the finding's own thread got no reply and was never resolved, so the thread holds no record of how it was handled.
